title: Morning Robotics Scan
report:
## Helix 2.5 Zero-Shot Home Generalization

### The Breakthrough
The team released Helix 2.5, a humanoid robot that tackles three long‑horizon household tasks across 30 unseen Bay Area homes without any environment‑specific data. By pretraining a single policy on the massive Index human‑behavior dataset, the robot attains 56 % success in blind tests, a six‑fold jump over a randomly initialized baseline. This demonstrates the first large‑scale zero‑shot whole‑body autonomy for a single platform.

### The Caveats
The claim is limited to one robot morphology and only three tasks, with no evaluation on other platforms or task families.

## Agile-WAM Tactile-Vision Control

### The Breakthrough
Agile‑WAM introduces a tactile‑vision World Action Model that fuses camera frames and tactile signals into a shared latent space and predicts multimodal action chunks. The model achieves a 29.4 % relative boost in real‑world success rates while running inference in just 11.9 ms, enabling low‑latency control for contact‑rich manipulation.

### The Caveats
The paper lacks comparisons to established baselines, leaving the magnitude of improvement uncertain.

## Workspace Models Memory Token

### The Breakthrough
The authors distill vision‑language model supervision into a compact ‘workspace token’ that encodes task‑relevant history, allowing policies to query this token instead of invoking heavy VLMs at runtime. Experiments on simulated and real robots show the token improves both computational efficiency and manipulation performance.

### The Caveats
No benchmark against existing robotic memory or VLM baselines is provided, so the significance of the gains cannot be quantified.

## Wonder Robotic Meal Assembly

### The Breakthrough
Wonder unveiled an end‑to‑end robotic line that automatically assembles complete meals, integrating manipulation with ingredient handling to create a fully automated food‑service pipeline.

### The Caveats
The announcement lacks any performance numbers, hardware specifications, or comparative analysis, making the claim of being the first such system unverified.

## UBTECH 10k-Unit Smart Factory

### The Breakthrough
UBTECH’s new 14,000 m² smart factory uses a digital ‘smart brain’ and a Siemens‑co‑developed operations system to schedule work orders, material flow, and traceability with one‑item‑one‑code IDs, enabling a reported production rate of one humanoid every ten minutes and a 50 % gain in storage density via a 65 m² stereoscopic warehouse.

### The Caveats
Independent verification of the ten‑minute per robot rate or overall throughput is absent, leaving the scalability claim unsubstantiated.

## FAMOS Articulation Modeling

### The Breakthrough
FAMOS presents a Feed‑Forward 3D Articulation Transformer that fuses sparse, unordered point clouds from multiple views to predict movable‑part segmentation and joint parameters, even from a single monocular observation, thanks to a novel articulation span supervision and a procedural data generator.

### The Caveats
All experiments are confined to simulated datasets; real‑world robot perception performance remains untested.

## SafeHarness Coding Agent Safety

### The Breakthrough
SafeHarness equips a language‑model‑based coding agent with obstacle‑aware route planning and contact execution modules, modeling objects as bounding boxes to generate and verify safe waypoints before execution. This yields 71.9 % task success and 87.5 % collision avoidance, a 6.5 % and 27 % improvement over the prior state‑of‑the‑art agent.

### The Caveats
Results are demonstrated only in simulation with static obstacles, with no physical robot validation.

## OpenHarness Coding Agent Platform

### The Breakthrough
OpenHarness is an open‑source framework that runs multiple coding agents in persistent tmux sessions and connects them to a desk‑side hardware device via encrypted WebRTC, allowing domain‑specific harnesses to add toolchains and live viewers without modifying core code.

### The Caveats
The platform is announced without benchmarks or formal evaluation, so its performance and generality are unverified.

### Priority
Helix 2.5 provides the first real‑world demonstration of zero‑shot whole‑body autonomy across dozens of homes, showing a tangible leap in general‑purpose robot capability.

### One action
Watch for follow‑up videos or datasets from Figure AI to explore applying large‑scale pretraining to other robot platforms.

### What to watch
Several items push manipulation forward: Agile‑WAM shows tactile‑vision latent modeling for faster control; Workspace Models offers lightweight memory tokens to reduce VLM overhead; SafeHarness focuses on safety in coding‑agent generated motions. Together they illustrate a trend toward integrating perception, memory, and safety primitives into embodied agents.
